text:
samir: quick heads-up — saw a regression on the LLProto path for the 8-GPU TF32 baseline. latency p95 up ~18% when batch_size=2, seq_len=1024. looks like allreduce time is spiking during decoder kv merge.

maya: can you paste the short perf snippet? is this on the LL/LL128 mix or pure PROTO? :eyes:

samir: pure PROTO fallback on most runs. nvprof/trace shows prolonged allreduce stalls right after kv-cache writeback. snippet below:

```
[PROFILE] step=1200, step_time=0.092s
  compute_forward: 0.034s
  kv_writeback: 0.008s
  allreduce: 0.041s  <-- unusually high
  post_sync: 0.009s
nv_gpu_util: 78%
nccl: algo=PROTO, channels=4, ll=disabled
```

comm-bot: [alert] NCCL policy triggered fallback -> PROTO (reason: channel allocation failure on channel 6)

leo: interesting — allreduce>compute could mean channel contention + algorithm change. are we seeing fragmentation of msgs (small msg churn) that pushes proto selection? any change in our chunking heuristics recently?

samir: yes, landed a micro-change in kernel selector last week to prefer smaller chunk sizes for >1024 seq to reduce latency in warmup cases. I suspected it might impact collective sizes.

anita: if chunk sizes shrank, message count increases and PROTO sometimes wins for lots of small messages. PROTO has more per-chunk overhead for our pattern. can you repro with chunk_override to force larger chunks?

samir: repro attached with ENV override:
```
export RW_CHUNK_SIZE=5120
run_profiler --model=decoder-only --gpus=8 --bs=2 --seq=1024
```

samir: with chunk_override=5120 I see allreduce drop to 0.018s and step_time back to 0.063s.

devon: that's a pretty clear signal. two immediate actions: (1) revert the micro-change or make it a tunable heuristic depending on parallelism profile; (2) add a probe in runtime that tracks avg_msg_size and forces a minimum chunk threshold when avg_msg_size < X to avoid proto.

maya: +1. also let's add a short unit test in perf-suite: simulate many small kv writes and assert NCCL doesn't pick PROTO for >4 channels unless msg_count < threshold.

leo: for a quick mitigation, can we bias the NCCL algo selector to prefer ALGO for messages in [4kB..64kB] on our hw? Might need to be per-device/family.

anita: yes but that becomes maintenance pain. low-risk patch: ensure our kernel selector exposes a "collective_friendly_chunk" flag when tensor-parallel shards > 1 and total_gpus >=8.

samir: filing an RFC now: rfc/2065000000-collective-aware-chunking.md (WIP). I'll include the trace and the chunk override repro commands. tagging @eng-runtime for visibility.

comm-bot: deploy-checklist updated: add e2e perf probe for chunking-change (flaky=false)

maya: can someone run the nsys long trace on a problematic rack to ensure we don't have NIC buffer pressure? I want to rule out interconnect queueing vs selector algorithm.

devon: I'll run on rack-7 tonight and post nsys summary tomorrow AM.

samir: thanks — goal is to get a short patch in next <=48h to flip heuristic behind a flag + perf-test. if that looks good we can roll canary on dedicated pools.

leo: SGTM. also capture kernel-level counters (PCIe TXQ lengths) in the probe so we can distinguish queueing vs message-size algo behavior.

anita: adding TODO in the RFC: telemetry fields to record avg_msg_size, chosen_nccl_algo, channels, ll_enabled, chunk_size. will help for future regressions.

samir: thanks all. will update thread with RFC link and test results.
